title: Launch brief — Console Usage Insights (Cost Drivers by Route/Model)
content:
Doc owner: Paula (PM)
Sponsor: Marissa
Last updated: 2026-02-21

1) What we are launching
Feature name (external): Usage Insights — Cost drivers by route
Feature name (internal): Console route/model usage insights + exports
Surface area:
- Redwood Console → Usage → Insights (new)
- Route list view: ranked spend + trend sparkline + quick filters
- Route detail view: model breakdown, p50/p95 latency, error rate, “what changed vs prior period”
- Export report: CSV + JSON, bounded by time range/row limits, audit logged

Scope highlights (GA):
- New telemetry dimensions: route + model (plus request attributes needed for top drivers)
- Aggregations and APIs: cost + performance by route/model across time windows
- Console UI shipped behind feature flag, with pagination/limits and empty states
- Export workflow (create job → download), RBAC enforced and audited
- Docs + SDK guidance for route identifiers (naming conventions, cardinality control)

Explicit non-goals for GA (keep messaging tight):
- Full anomaly detection/alerts (beyond “change vs prior period”)
- Customer-defined custom dimensions beyond route/model
- Long-term historical exports beyond retention policy

2) Why this matters / customer value
Primary customer question we answer:
- “What routes are costing us the most?”
- “Which models drive spend on those routes?”
- “What changed week-over-week and why?”
- “Can I export something Finance/Ops can use in incident + cost reviews?”

Value prop (positioning):
- Fast route-level cost attribution for engineering teams + FinOps
- Actionable breakdowns (route → model) to target optimization (cache/batching/model choice)
- Trust + governance: export auditing and RBAC for enterprise workflows

3) Target audiences & personas
External:
A) AI/Platform engineers (primary)
- Wants: top cost drivers, route naming best practices, quickly identifying regressions
- CTA: tag routes in SDK/gateway, review top routes weekly, export for reviews

B) Eng managers / product leads
- Wants: spend transparency by feature/endpoint, “what changed” summaries
- CTA: use route ranking + deltas to prioritize optimization work

C) FinOps / Ops
- Wants: exports usable for internal chargeback and cost reviews, predictable schemas
- CTA: export bounded report, join with internal service ownership tables

D) Security/Compliance stakeholders (enterprise)
- Wants: RBAC boundaries, audit logs, retention controls
- CTA: review export audit events + retention docs; confirm least-privileged access

Internal:
- Sales/SE: demo flow + security/RBAC answers
- Support/CS: invoice mismatch FAQ, “Unknown route” guidance, export limits/troubleshooting
- Finance: interpretation of cached token fields + timing/freshness caveats

4) Beta plan
Objectives:
- Validate that route grouping and top-drivers UI matches how customers think about their apps
- Validate export workflow for Finance/Ops (schema completeness, limits acceptable)
- Shake out edge cases: missing route tags, multi-model fallback attribution, late-arriving metering

Entry criteria (beta):
- Telemetry pipeline emitting route + model for >= 95% of requests in at least one environment
- Basic cardinality guardrails enabled (length/character rules + unknown bucket behavior)
- RBAC enforced for insights endpoints and exports
- Audit logging events implemented for export create/download
- SRE dashboards live for pipeline lag + export failures

Beta cohorts:
- Cohort 0 (internal dogfood): Redwood production + staging
  - Goals: validate data correctness, UI performance, and export job stability
  - Timeline: late Feb → early Mar

- Cohort 1 (design partners, 5–8 orgs): mix of Hosted and Dedicated
  - Selection criteria:
    - demonstrated need for route-level chargeback or optimization
    - willingness to tag routes (SDK/gateway) and provide weekly feedback
    - at least one enterprise-style org with strict RBAC/audit expectations
  - Timeline: Mar (Weeks 7–8 in the project plan)

- Cohort 2 (expanded beta): up to 25 orgs
  - Gate: stable SLO + support readiness + export job success rate target met

Beta feedback loop:
- Weekly 30-min feedback call (Markus + Paula + Eng as needed)
- Asynchronous tracker (Drive sheet: usage-insights-beta-feedback-tracker)
- Success criteria to exit beta:
  - Customers can identify top 3 routes by spend without help
  - At least 2 customers successfully use export in a cost review workflow
  - No P0/P1 correctness issues outstanding (see “GA checklist”) 

5) GA plan / rollout strategy
Target GA: Console release window April 2026 (align with “Console 2026.04” release notes)
Rollout model:
- Phase 1: Feature flag on for beta orgs only
- Phase 2: Gradual enablement by org (batch enable 10/day) with monitoring gates
- Phase 3: Default-on for all orgs on supported plans (plan gating TBD; see Packaging)

Feature flags (proposed):
- console_usage_insights_routes_v1 (UI navigation + views)
- usage_insights_exports_v1 (export job + download)
- usage_insights_hourly_rollups_v1 (if we ship hourly in GA; otherwise keep daily-only)

6) GA checklist (launch gate)
A) Data correctness & product expectations
- Route definition finalized (SDK-provided vs gateway-derived precedence documented)
- “Unknown route” behavior documented and tested (missing tag cases)
- Multi-model fallback attribution verified: cost attributed to original route; model breakdown reflects actual execution
- Late-arriving metering: UI messaging for freshness (e.g., “data may update within X hours”) agreed with PM + SRE
- Known mismatch guidance published (console vs invoice timing/rounding/retention)

B) Cardinality guardrails
- Route normalization enforced (length limits, allowed chars, trimming)
- Limits for distinct routes per org/project/time window defined; overflow behavior defined (hash bucket/rollup)
- Docs include “DO NOT” examples (userId/orderId in route)
- Cardinality alerting enabled + runbook linked

C) Performance, reliability, and SLOs
- Insights API p95 latency meets target under load (per SLO doc)
- Query cost budgets enforced (pagination, max lookback, max group-bys)
- Export job success rate target met in beta (>= 99% for bounded exports)
- Export generation time within guardrails; timeouts + retries validated
- Dashboards live: pipeline lag, aggregation job latency, export failures, API error rates

D) Security & compliance
- RBAC verified end-to-end (org/project scoping + no cross-project leakage tests)
- Audit log events emitted for:
  - export job created
  - export file downloaded
  - export job failed (optional but recommended for evidence)
- Audit event fields include: actor, org/project, time range, filters, format, row count/size, IP/user agent (where available)
- Retention documented: exports availability window + where stored + residency behavior

E) Docs & DevEx
- Docs published:
  - Route tagging guide across SDKs / gateway
  - Usage insights overview + FAQs
  - Export schema + limits + troubleshooting
- Quickstart updated with minimal route tagging snippet and “verify in console” steps

F) Support & CS readiness
- Support macros drafted:
  - invoice mismatch explanation
  - “Unknown route” dominating top routes
  - export time range/timeout limitations
- Known issues page published and shared internally
- Escalation path defined (oncall rotation or Slack channel) for first 2 weeks post-GA

G) Analytics / success metrics
- Instrument Console usage insights pageviews, export job creation/download events
- Adoption targets (first 30 days post-GA; provisional):
  - 25% of active orgs visit Usage Insights at least once
  - 10% of active orgs export at least one report
  - Median “Unknown route” share decreases over time among orgs using SDK tagging

7) Packaging / pricing notes (TBD — decision needed)
Recommendation (initial):
- Insights views available to all paid plans (to drive tagging + trust)
- Exports gated by plan tier and/or limited quota (row count/time range)
  - Rationale: exports drive ops workflows and have clear compute cost
Open question: Should Dedicated/Private include higher export limits by default? (action: align with Product + Sales by mid-March)

8) Communications plan
External comms (GA):
- Release notes entry (Console 2026.04)
- Docs launch (2–3 pages + FAQ)
- In-product “What’s new” card (for org admins / developers)
- Optional: blog post or benchmark-style post (only if we have strong before/after cost optimization story)

Beta comms:
- Direct email to beta org admins (template owned by Paula; reviewed by CS)
- Console banner/tooltips for tagging guidance (“Set route IDs to unlock route-level insights”)

Messaging pillars:
- “See what’s driving spend by route, and which models are behind it.”
- “Export finance-ready reports (CSV/JSON) with RBAC and audit logging.”
- “Built for production realities: caching/cached tokens surfaced; late data handled transparently.”

Key disclaimers we should state clearly (and consistently across docs + UI):
- Console insights may lag real-time usage by up to X hours (final value depends on metering pipeline)
- Invoice reconciliation may not be exact due to timing, rounding, retention windows, and adjustments
- Export limits: bounded time ranges/row caps; no scheduled exports in GA

Internal comms:
- Announce beta availability in #announcements + #sales and link enablement
- Internal dogfood request: ask teams to set route tags in internal services and report issues

9) Internal enablement needs
Sales/SE enablement:
- 1-page demo script:
  - Route list → click route → model breakdown → export
  - How to answer: “Is export audit logged?” and “Can you do scheduled exports?”
- Security FAQ snippet:
  - RBAC model + audit event examples + retention/residency notes

CS/Support enablement:
- Triage guide:
  - cost mismatch cases
  - missing route tags / unknown route
  - export failures/timeouts
- Known issues doc (living) + escalation owners

Finance enablement:
- Short explainer: cached tokens and GPU-time proxy fields (if shown) and what to do with them
- Suggested internal workflow: export → join with route ownership mapping → monthly chargeback

10) Risks / watchouts (launch)
- Cardinality blow-ups from dynamic route strings
  - Mitigation: strict normalization + docs + alarms + overflow buckets

- Perceived correctness issues (invoice mismatch)
  - Mitigation: consistent FAQ messaging + explicit freshness window + support macro

- Export job performance under large time ranges
  - Mitigation: hard limits + guided UX + pagination + preflight estimates (future)

- Confusion around model fallback attribution
  - Mitigation: UI copy + tooltip explaining “model breakdown reflects executed models; routing may change model for reliability”

11) Owners / next actions
- GA date + packaging decision: Marissa + Paula (by 2026-03-10)
- Beta org list + outreach: Markus + CS (by 2026-03-05)
- Docs completion + screenshots: Elliot + Wei (by 2026-03-20)
- SLOs finalized + alerts enabled: Allison (by 2026-03-15)
- Security review sign-off (RBAC + audit logs): Naomi + Kevin (by 2026-03-18)
- Support macros + known issues: Dev (by 2026-03-22)

Appendix: Open questions
- Do we ship hourly rollups in GA or keep daily-only for cost/perf stability?
- Export schema versioning: how do we add fields without breaking automation? (proposal: include schema_version column + changelog)
- Are route tags customer-editable/mutable post-hoc? If not, ensure docs and UI make this clear.
